feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: The planned public execution has been canceled, but what message did it send?
entry.summary: President Trump announced that the Fort Hood attacker's execution will not be livestreamed. NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with New Yorker journalist Dexter Filkins, who witnessed a public execution.

entry.title: U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history
entry.summary: Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law, fueling a backlash that critics say is as fiery as the one that led to the law's creation 60 years ago.

entry.title: Trump cancels public execution, but a line may already have been crossed
entry.summary: Defense Secretary Hegseth's announcement of a livestreamed execution elicited reactions of disgust and condemnation from some faith leaders and politicians. But within his church, it's not an outlier.

entry.title: LA fire survivors face another setback with FEMA program delays
entry.summary: The fight over a FEMA program aiding some of LA's most vulnerable wildfire victims is the latest setback for hundreds of fire survivors who still haven't rebuilt after the deadly 2025 infernos.

entry.title: Social Security could soon run out of money. Here are some possible solutions
entry.summary: Social Security may run short of money to make full payments to retirees as soon as 2032. The team from NPR's Planet Money examines possible solutions.

entry.title: Wyoming tribes ask church pastor to leave after viral sermon
entry.summary: Tribes on the Wind River Reservation in Wyoming are asking a Christian pastor to leave after she denigrated their native religion in a sermon.

entry.title: USS Abraham Lincoln returns home as Navy navigates lengthy deployments among crews
entry.summary: The crew of USS Abraham Lincoln is now home, tired and ready for the next chapter. But the Navy is grappling with crews still at sea with lengthy deployments as the U.S. war with Iran continues.

entry.title: A rocky first press briefing for a rookie White House press secretary
entry.summary: Katie Zacharia's first White House press briefing was short and often halting. The new press secretary chosen by President Trump left a lot of unanswered questions, including some uncertainties about her own qualifications.

entry.title: Cornell's president has not resigned despite heavy scrutiny
entry.summary: The president of Cornell University, Michael Kotlikoff, is under fire over the university's handling of a gang rape at a fraternity party in 2024.

entry.title: 'They're stealing from the poor': A major source of SNAP fraud robs recipients of millions
entry.summary: Organized criminal rings target SNAP recipients because of the government program's outdated security features. But upgrading the tech costs money and states' SNAP budgets are getting squeezed.
